sections.html: The animal presented here strongly resembles Awaous lateristriga, but it could not yet be determined whether it is identical to this species. With an overall length of approx. 30 cm, Awaous lateristriga is one of the larger gobies.
The freshwater goby Awaous lateristriga originates from the coastal ranges of western Africa between Senegal and Angola.
In their habitat they inhabit freshwater biotopes such as swamps, flooded fields and periodically draining rivers, and also brackish water biotopes.

Since they are imported only very rarely, nearly nothing is known about their maintenance in aquaria. Related species such as Awaous flavus are kept occasionally in aquariums and also bred in some rare cases. A changing salinity of the water plays a crucial role in their maintenance and breeding. This corresponds to their life cycle: the larvae are born in fresh water, then drift passively in the sea or in estuaries, in order to ascend into fresh water again after some months. The adults then live there and the reproduction cycle starts again.
